2.  This writ petition has been filed for the following reliefs:
"(i) For issuance of an appropriate writ, order or direction, directing the respondent authorities to show cause as to how and under what circumstance, the compensation amount in lieu of acquisition of the land for Subarnrekha Project, Mango, Town Jamshedpur pertaining to Plot no.477 under Khata no.82, corresponding to old Plot no.187 under old Khata no.49, measuring an area of 30.5 decimals; plot no.578 under Khata no.83, corresponding to old Plot no.182 under old Khata no.5, measuring an area of 33 decimals; and Plot no.481 under Khata no.82, corresponding to Old Plot no.368 under old Khata no.49, measuring an area of 4 decimals; total area 67.5 decimals of land at Mouja Kamarigora; has not been paid to the petitioner till date;

sentences.text:
(ii) Upon showing no cause or insufficient cause, further for issuance of an appropriate writ, order or direction, directing the respondent authorities to pay the compensation amount along with statutory interest in respect of acquisition of the aforesaid land of the petitioner for Subarnrekha Project, Mango, Town Jamshedpur in terms of the provision of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (hereinafter to be referred as 'the Act, 2013); and (iii) For any other relief or reliefs for which the petitioner is legally entitled in the facts and circumstances of the case."
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the petitioner is claiming property involved in the present case by virtue of registered sale deed dated 30.04.1962 executed in the name of his father.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: He has also submitted that all other connected documents including revenue records are in favour of the petitioner.

The learned counsel submits that the State in the counter-affidavit has filed an Award in connection with the property being Land Acquisition Case No.25 of 2015-2016 and the award has been prepared, inter alia, in the name of the vendor of the property, who had executed the sale deed dated 30.04.1962 and also in favour of other persons relating with the Khata number and plot number.
4.

The learned counsel submits that the vendor / legal heirs and successors of the property have instituted a title suit being Title Suit No. 38 of 2018 seeking a declaration that the sale deed dated 30.04.1962 is itself null and void, which is the reason for non- disbursement of amount to the petitioner.

Learned counsel submits that the award itself has been wrongly prepared in the name of vendor and therefore, the petitioner is seeking a mandamus upon the respondents for release of compensation to the petitioner, who is the owner of the property, even as per the counter-affidavit filed by the respondents.
5. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the State, on the other hand, has submitted that the Award has been brought on record which is admittedly not in favour of the petitioner.

He has also submitted that if there is any error in the award, then the grievance of the petitioner has to be looked into by the respondent no.4 and before making any modification in connection with the Award, the persons in whose favour the Award has been prepared, are also required to be heard.

In case of any dispute regarding title or entitlement of compensation, the matter has to be decided by competent court of civil jurisdiction, but the aforesaid exercise has to be first undertaken by the respondent no.4.

He also submits that even the persons who are claiming property and have instituted the title suit, are not party before this Court and therefore, the relief as prayed for by the petitioner seeking a mandamus for release of compensation be not issued.

6. After hearing the learned counsel for the parties, it appears that the petitioner is claiming that certain property, which was purchased by his father by virtue of registered sale deed dated 30.04.1962, has been acquired, but the award has been prepared in favour of the vendor of the property.
Admittedly, the award has not been prepared in the name of the petitioner.

sentences.text: It is the case of the petitioner that the Award has been wrongly prepared, inter alia, in the name of vendor of the sale deed dated 30.04.1962 and further the vendor /his successor in interest has instituted a title suit for cancellation of the sale deed.

8. The fact remains that the award has not been prepared in the name of the petitioner and therefore, this Court is not inclined to issue a mandamus upon the respondents to release any compensation arising out of such award.
Even the persons in whose favour the award has been prepared in connection with the property claimed by the petitioner are not party in this writ petition.

9. However, this writ petition is disposed of enabling the petitioner to approach the respondent no.4 by filing a detailed representation along with connected documents raising his grievance in connection with the award within a period of three weeks from today.

Upon filing of such representation, the respondent no.4 shall consider the grievance of the petitioner after granting an opportunity of hearing to the persons in whose favour the award has been prepared and pass a reasoned order in accordance with law within a period of six weeks from the date of filing of the representation.

10. In case any dispute is raised before the respondent no.4 regarding title/entitlement of compensation, the respondent no.4 shall further do the needful within a period of two weeks from the date of the reasoned order so that the dispute in connection with the entitlement of compensation is taken to a logical end.

The reasoned order be communicated to the parties through speed post at the address to be provided by them before the respondent no.4.
11.
Pending interlocutory application, if any, stands closed.

(Anubha Rawat Choudhary, J.) Saurav/
